$comment: One description of the raw-XML escape-hatch session ops and how each transport names them (issue #982). SessionOpDescriptionDriftTests checks every transport against it; see docs/architecture/session_op_descriptions.md. Argument names are the canonical wire names; argNames, defaults, requires and absent on a transport are recorded divergences, not the target. The Python methods live on the session's raw sub-proxy (session.raw.get_xml and so on).

npm.absent: not a DocxSession method by design: grouped on the session's raw property (raw.getXml) so raw XML access is explicit at the call site

mcp.absent: kept off by design: MCP gives an agent typed, validated edits only, so raw OOXML stays off the agent surface

npm.absent: not a DocxSession method by design: grouped on the session's raw property (raw.insertXml) so raw XML access is explicit at the call site

mcp.absent: kept off by design: MCP gives an agent typed, validated edits only; inserting raw OOXML would bypass that

npm.absent: not a DocxSession method by design: grouped on the session's raw property (raw.replaceXml) so raw XML access is explicit at the call site

mcp.absent: kept off by design: MCP gives an agent typed, validated edits only; replacing raw OOXML would bypass that
